A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same REMI-z tokenizer and reconstruction-based music arrangement framework. All pages, including both versions' appendices and v3's checklist, support comparison. Renamed, reordered and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original tokenizer measurements, objective and human evaluations of three arrangement tasks, ablations, and instrument and chord probing experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including the appendix probing experiments, and adds statistical reporting.

M1.justification: The REMI-z ordering, model architecture, reconstruction objective, instrument/content/history conditions and task-specific procedures remain unchanged. Appendix B.2 specifies the sampling details of track deletion already described in v2; it does not establish a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Los Angeles MIDI corpus, Slakh2100, three arrangement tasks, out-of-domain band settings and probing tasks. The clearer piano-accompaniment wording in v3 matches the scope already explained in v2 Appendix B.3.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Transformer-VAE, UNet, Composer's Assistant v2, the same rule-based references, REMI+, and the same ablation and probing comparators. Expanded UNet implementation disclosures do not establish a changed comparator.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 revises the stated Slakh2100 minimum from five to four tracks per piece. Dataset split counts, model sizes, training budgets, segment lengths and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. This is a reported setting revision, without evidence that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The pre-training, voice and history ablations, instrument and chord probes, out-of-domain band evaluation, and UNet octave-shift analysis are retained. The newly documented deletion procedure and survey screenshots add no new ablation or robustness experiment.

E5.justification: v3 Tables 2–4 first report standard errors for human ratings, and Section 4.3/Table 1 add Wilcoxon signed-rank significance testing for the tokenizer comparison. Repeated-measures ANOVA and the fixed training seed of 42 were already reported; additional training runs are not established.

E6.justification: Matched performance-table means and probing scores are unchanged. However, v3 introduces prose discrepancies: Section 5.3 gives creativity 3.47 and phrase transition 3.27, while both versions' tables give 3.27 and 3.77. Section 5.2 newly calls 3.86 the highest playability score despite Rule-O's retained 4.07. These are changed reported values and rankings, not performance gains.

T1.justification: The reconstruction equation and mathematical metric definitions are retained. Entropy and perplexity equations move from v2 Section 4.2 to v3 Appendix C.2 without substantive mathematical revision. Neither version contains theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The unified framework, tokenizer benefits and superiority claims on the same three tasks remain. v3 removes the explicit headline contribution about pre-training's crucial role in longer, complex-alignment tasks, while foregrounding the existing framework's token-level disentanglement and flexible instrumentation transfer.

C2.justification: New Appendix G substantially expands applicability qualifications: pop-focused evaluation, identical input/output structure, absent global instrument planning and fixed creativity control. It also explicitly discusses melody-retention failures. Appendix F adds substantive discussion of Western-music bias and possible downstream applications beyond v2's narrower caveats.

D1.justification: v3 adds the Poisson track-deletion rule, clipping and sampling details; clarifies UNet adaptation and metric aggregation; and discloses 26 listeners, musical experience, Cubase AI 13 rendering and session duration. The checklist adds dataset-license and supplementary-code information. These principally document existing experiments.

R1.justification: v3 adds references including Byte Pair Encoding for Symbolic Music, MIDI-GPT and NotaGen, and positions vocabulary compression as complementary to REMI-z. It removes the dedicated NLP prompting discussion and associated citations. The principal music-arrangement predecessors and comparisons remain.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and results narrative are extensively rewritten. Reconstruction precedes tokenization in the method section, tokenizer results move after task results, and related work is reorganized. v3 also changes the title and author list and adds impact, limitations and checklist sections, although unfinished acknowledgment-template prose remains.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. v2 Figure 2 is split into v3 Figures 1–2, the vocabulary table moves to Appendix A, and result tables gain metric-direction arrows and uncertainty displays. v3 Figure 6 adds survey screenshots; most other visual content is retained and rearranged.

improvement.justification: v3 improves transparency through reproducible deletion details, fuller human-study documentation, uncertainty reporting and concrete applicability limits. These help readers assess the retained evidence. New numerical and ranking errors in the results prose, plus unfinished acknowledgment-template text, temper the benefit. The overall gain is limited to documentation and interpretation; the method and tabulated performance remain unchanged.
